correctness.rationale: Exact inverse branches show \(h(0)=h(1)=0\), \(h'(1)=-Ah(1/2)\), and \(h'(0)=ABh(1/2)/(1-B)\). The endpoint integrals are quadratic. Uniform expansion, bounded-variation inverse-branch weights, and finite-branch small-hole Lasota–Yorke estimates yield the Keller–Liverani assumptions, including the essential \(O(\varepsilon)O(\varepsilon)=O(\mu(H_\varepsilon))\) condition. The only nonzero limiting finite-time first return is the fixed-endpoint immediate factor \(B=\sum p_j\Lambda_j^{-2}\); the opposite endpoint has none. Keller–Liverani therefore yields exact quadratic escape coefficients and their ratio. CHECK.py reconstructs inverse maps and verifies exact rational identities and finite-grid spectra, but finite testing is not an infinite proof.
